ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a 3 V voltage source, with its bottom end connected to the common lower wire; above it there are, in sequence, switch S1, a node, and switch S2. The middle node is connected through capacitor C1 to the common wire below, and the figure labels C1 = 1 F. The right-side node is connected through capacitor C2 to the same common lower wire, and the figure labels C2 = 2 F. Therefore the lower plates of the two capacitors share the lower wire, S1 can connect the upper end of C1 to the 3 V power supply, and S2 can connect the upper ends of C1 and C2 together. Reasoning: When t < 0, S1 is closed and S2 is open, so C1 is connected across the 3 V power supply, its initial voltage is 3 V, and the charge Q1 = C1 V1 = 1 F × 3 V = 3 C. At this time C2 is disconnected from C1, and the problem gives VC2(0) = 0, so Q2 = C2 V2 = 2 F × 0 V = 0 C. At t = 0, S1 opens and S2 closes, the power supply is disconnected from the capacitor combination, and C1 and C2 become connected in parallel. Ideally, according to charge conservation, the common voltage V after the two capacitors are connected in parallel satisfies (C1 + C2)V = Q1 + Q2 = 3 C. Therefore V = 3 / (1 + 2) = 1 V.
